rv.q: “Oh, Mary!” is a welcome diversion — a revisionist lark with an irreverent LGBTQ+ spirit.
Oh, Mary! is outrageous, inventive, hysterically funny, and unlike almost anything else currently touring.
Escola's mega-hit, Tony Award winning and Pulitzer Prize nominated show will keep you in stitches for its entire 90-minute run.
Oh, Mary! is a sundae of American history gone cheerfully off the rails, and it leaves us begging for one more scoop.
Cole Escola’s wildly absurd, historically inaccurate farce has made its way from Broadway to the national tour, and the transition works beautifully.
Alaska's Mary is glitzy, unpredictable and laugh-out-loud funny, but she is also more relatable—and more perceptive—than she initially lets on.
Ireland’s play remains a brave and expertly crafted piece of writing.
What follows is 80 minutes of crass, rude fun that is absolutely one of the most original comedies to come along in a very long time.

Oh, Mary! is stupendously funny, bursting with talent, and packed with more laughs than most comedies manage in twice the running time; it's the kind of theatrical experience that leaves you walking out of the theater buzzing, grinning, and already wishing you could see it again.
It is offensive and raunchy in the best way possible.
Thunderfuck is fearless in bringing the narcissistic, boozy, brazen, and ever stagestruck Mary to hilariously unhinged life, not to mention revealing a talent I’m forbidden to discuss in this review.
Oh, Mary! more than lives up to its reputation.
As feisty and foul-mouthed and queer and outrageous as “Oh, Mary!” ecstatically is, small theaters will be clamoring to do this show for decades.
Thunderf**k’s physical agility, even in hoop skirts, is mesmerizing, especially because it's combined with impeccable comic timing.
“Oh, Mary!” proves itself to be hilarious, vulgar, absurd — and very legitimate theatre.
But I can say I've never heard an audience at the Civic Theatre roar with more suprised laughter than I did on on Wednesday, the official opening night of the Broadway play's national tour.
Oh, Mary! was unlike anything I'd seen onstage before.
I loved every laugh-filled moment of it.

The play, a 2025. Pulitzer Prize in Drama finalist, is mighty bold and wonderfully irreverent, following a fictional, highly inaccurate version of the first lady in the weeks leading up to Abraham Lincoln's assassination.
The intense campiness that permeates the production is marvelously good fun...
Alaska’s performance takes the tiara.
What's brilliant about Escola's tightly constructed, 75-minute play is that, even with all the raunchy jokes and camp sensibility, it sits just on the edgier fringe of mainstream humor...
Unexpected SNL-style deadpans and a hilariously unhinged spin on gay history.
"Oh, Mary!" delivers plenty of chuckles but few belly laughs.
“Oh, Mary!” achieves the kind of rarified hilarity that makes you laugh in anticipation of laughing.
Oh, Mary! is a farcical delight that revels in the incredible comic timing of underrated drag queen Alaska Thunderfuck.
This is a not-to-be missed show which catches up to its hype in a big way.

cn.t: Critics overwhelmingly praise *Oh, Mary!* as a riotously funny, gleefully unhinged farce, with Alaska Thunderfuck's commanding comic performance earning particular acclaim. One outlier calls it "so-so," but the consensus is clear: the hype is justified.
